definition: The sky or vault of heaven; the upper air considered as a visible expanse, especially when dramatic or expressive of weather — as in the old cry 'make the welkin ring,' meaning to fill the very sky with sound.
etymology: From Old English wolcen, meaning cloud or sky, itself from Proto-Germanic wulkną. The word drifted through Middle English as welken, shedding its cloud-specific sense and broadening to embrace the whole dome overhead. Cousin to the Dutch wolk and German Wolke, both still meaning cloud — English kept the sky and gave away the rain.
usage: Late August suits it perfectly: stand outside at dusk when the welkin goes from brass to violet in ten minutes and you will not reach for a blander word.
